figures.caption: The design and sequences of rattusin fragments based on its three-dimensional structure. (a) The identification of fragment regions in the rattusin structure, with F1 (residues 1–8), F2 (residues 12–18), F3 (residues 22–31), and F4 (residues 7–23) highlighted in the full rattusin tertiary structure. The N-terminus (N) and C-terminus (C) are indicated for each fragment. (b) The primary sequences of the rattusin fragments alongside schematic diagrams representing the amino acid sequences and positions. Each fragment is depicted with its corresponding segment of the rattusin molecule, with disulfide bonds illustrated by lines connecting the cysteine residues.
figures.label: Figure 1

figures.caption: The time course of membrane depolarization in S. aureus induced by the antimicrobial peptide rattusin, its derivative fragment F2, and the control peptides melittin and buforin-2. Depolarization was monitored using the fluorescent DiSC(3)-5 dye. The arrows indicate the points of dye and peptide addition.
figures.label: Figure 2

figures.caption: SYTOX Green uptake assay monitoring the permeabilization of S. aureus cell membranes by peptides. The concentrations of the peptides used in the experiment were 32 µM for F2, 4 µM for melittin, and 16 µM for buforin-2.
figures.label: Figure 3

figures.caption: Assay of ONPG hydrolysis by peptides using E. coli ML-35. The concentrations of the peptides used in the experiment were 32 µM for F2, 4 µM for melittin, and 16 µM for buforin-2.
figures.label: Figure 4

figures.caption: The DNA-binding activity of peptides assessed by the gel retardation assay. Gel electrophoresis illustrating the DNA-binding capability of peptides. The retarded bands signify successful DNA binding, observable for buforin-2 at 2 μM and F2 at 4 μM. No retardation was evident for the monomeric F2 (C15S) up to 16 μM.
figures.label: Figure 5

figures.caption: Cytotoxicity analysis of peptide F2. (a) Hemolysis assay results displaying the percentage of hemolysis of sheep RBCs after treatment with increasing concentrations of peptide F2 and melittin. (b) MTT assay results showing cell viability percentages for Hs68 and HeLa cells upon treatment with varying concentrations of peptide F2.
figures.label: Figure 6
